neighbours.label: a word marking a past state that contrasts with the present ('which it wasn't then', 'non-existent before ... now')
fire: The town has a hospital now, which it wasn't lucky enough to have in 1950.
The path is lit at night now, which it wasn't when I was a student.
Smartphones, which were non-existent twenty years ago, are now in every pocket.
The river is clean now, which it wasn't during the factory years.
Online banking, which was virtually non-existent before 1995, is now routine.
The school is free now, which it wasn't when my mother went there.
Organic food, which was almost non-existent in local shops, is now common.
The station is accessible now, which it wasn't until last year.
quiet: The town has a hospital, a library and two primary schools.
The path is lit at night and patrolled by guards.
Smartphones are now in every pocket and cost less each year.
The river is clean and full of fish in the summer.
Online banking is routine for most customers today.
The school is free and open to all local children.
Organic food is common in local shops these days.
The station is accessible and has a lift on each platform.

notes: Probe: 'which it wasn't when' 0.82, 'non-existent before the war, are now' 0.76, 'was once covered' 0.31; 'formerly' 0.05, present-only controls 0.01-0.04. + pole is ' once' / 'formerly'.
